course_description:
This course discusses relevant issues in the management of people, including motivation, groups and teams, emotions and stress, individual differences, leadership and organisation change.

Why do some teams thrive while others fall apart? Why do talented individuals sometimes underperform, while others exceed expectations? Organisational Behaviour (OB) offers a powerful lens for understanding the human side of work — and this course puts those insights directly in your hands.

Over twelve weeks, you will explore a rich set of topics spanning the individual, group, and organisational levels, including personality and values, motivation, emotions and stress, group dynamics, decision making, creativity and innovation, power and ethics, conflict and negotiation, leadership, organisational culture, and change. Each topic has been carefully selected to help you better understand yourself and others, and to make you a more effective manager, collaborator, and leader.

Each week combines a one-hour lecture focused on key theories and concepts with a two-hour interactive workshop where you will apply those ideas through simulations, case studies, and collaborative exercises.

To get the most out of this course, engage with the learning resources consistently and on a weekly basis, including this course profile, the Blackboard page, and communications from course staff.

course_aims: This course examines research on the management of people, at the individual, interpersonal, and organisational levels. A major focus of the course is to introduce different perspectives for managing people, understanding the nature of organisations, and the determinants of of productive and unproductive behaviour in organisations.

learning_outcomes.description: Identify prominent theories and models about human behaviour in organisations, and critically discuss their application to management.
Identify prominent theories and models of group functioning in organisations, and critically discuss their significance in workplaces.
As an individual and in groups, explain how organisations function as institutions including issues of structure, power, politics, and change.
Critically examine your own behaviour as a manager, and identify strategies for improving your skills in people management.
Reflect on the ethical and social impact of managing people within organisations.

assessment_details.due_date: Presentation Slides - 5PM - 4/09/2026 Presentation Week 7 - Week 8 Presentation during your allocated tutorial.
assessment_details.other_conditions: Time limited, Peer assessed. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: In this assessment, you will work in a randomly assigned team of 4–5 students to select a real organisation facing a current problem or opportunity that has appeared in the media within the last twelve months, and deliver a 10-minute presentation analysing the issue through the lens of organisational behaviour theory. Your presentation (10–15 PowerPoint slides) must identify the organisational issue, analyse it using 2 or more OB concepts/theories from Weeks 2–6 (3 or more for a higher grade), and provide evidence-based recommendations, supported by at least 7 peer-reviewed references. One group member must submit the slides via Blackboard by the due date, and presentations are delivered during your allocated tutorial in Weeks 7–8 using brief notes only. After presenting, each member must complete a peer evaluation via BuddyCheck, which may be used to adjust individual marks. This assessment aims to demonstrate your ability to collaborate as a team to apply key OB theories to a real-world organisational challenge of your own choosing. Please Note: The presentation will be recorded for marking purposes per UQ Policy. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
Submission guidelines:
One group member needs to submit the slides as a PDF or PowerPoint document using the assessment submission link in Blackboard. Please include your group number/name and workshop session in the file name (e.g., “A1_Group6_Tue8am.pptx”). Your marker will not mark your assessment if it is not submitted through Blackboard. During your presentation, the presenter may use brief notes only; do not read to the class. After your presentation, each member will need to complete Buddycheck on Blackboard. This peer evaluation will be used to adjust individual group assignment results if needed.
Additional details are on the course Blackboard site, under the "Assessment" folder. Please also refer to the regular announcements on Blackboard.

assessment_details.title: Critical Incident Reflection Essay (Individual)
assessment_details.task_description: In this individual assessment, you will write a reflective essay drawing on your experience of Assessment 1, identifying at least 3 critical incidents from the preparation and delivery of your group presentation and analysing each using a different OB concept or theory from Weeks 2–10. For each incident, you will describe its significance, evaluate the relational dynamics at play, apply relevant OB theory, and examine the ethical dimensions of your team's behaviour. You will also reflect on your growth as a team performer and propose at least two developmental activities framed as acts of responsible leadership. Your reflection should go beyond description to critically analyse both your individual and team contributions, supported by specific examples and evidence. An AI disclosure statement must be included at the end of the essay. This assessment aims to develop your ability to critically reflect on real team experiences through the lens of OB theory, deepening your understanding of how these frameworks apply to workplace dynamics.
